--------
In this VladTV interview, Tito “TJ” Dominguez recounts the high-risk shift from marijuana runs between Miami, the Bahamas and Colombia to cocaine transportation in the early 1980s. After a botched airdrop left him owing $800,000 to Colombian traffickers from La Guajira, Dominguez says he was kidnapped in Kendall, south of Miami, and given 24 hours to pay. His solution: fly a Beechcraft-style plane he called “Gigi,” the “Gray Ghost,” to move 450 kilos of cocaine — an event he says later appeared in one of his indictments.

Dominguez also describes meeting Pablo Escobar, Gustavo, and Escobar’s Miami representative Ramirez, negotiating kilo rates, using radios and code names like “Ciclón,” and securing a Bahamas airport through bribery. The conversation offers a firsthand look at drug smuggling logistics, cartel pressure, and the dangerous line between marijuana trafficking and the cocaine trade.

In this VladTV interview, Rene “Boxer” Enriquez recounts his years inside California prisons while carrying out orders tied to the Mexican Mafia. Enriquez explains why failed prison attacks were still judged by intent, describing a “PC move” and how inmates were punished if they appeared to avoid doing the job. He details a second attempted hit on Ronald Hayward, connected to a conflict involving Darrell Baca from Artesia and Bogle motorcycle associates, before being transferred from Tracy to Folsom State Prison.

Enriquez also recalls sharing a cell with Mexican Mafia member Sammy Balboa, later killed in Long Beach in 2019, and being drawn into a prison race war involving Black inmates, Crips/Piru factions, and Aryan Brotherhood prisoners. Despite three separate attacks ordered or approved within that world, all three targets survived, shaping Enriquez’s path deeper into the system’s SHU politics.
